prompt: Assess this claim: Indigenous people have lower average life expectancy than the national average.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is **generally supported in many countries, but needs a country and time period to be precise**. Indigenous populations in countries such as Australia, Canada, and New Zealand have lower average life expectancy than their respective national populations.

The size of the gap varies across Indigenous communities, regions, and years. It reflects factors including unequal access to healthcare, poverty, discrimination, and the lasting effects of colonisation; Indigenous identity itself is not an explanation.

A more precise version is: “In many countries, Indigenous populations have lower average life expectancy than the national average, although the gap varies by population and period.”
